newsitem.title: ITALY: Santer says expects Italy in first EMU wave - paper.
newsitem.headline: Santer says expects Italy in first EMU wave - paper.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer was quoted on Tuesday saying that Rome's latest efforts to clean up state finances meant Italy should be a founder member of the planned single European currency.

Earlier this year, the Commission questioned whether Italy would meet the criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty for euro aspirants, but Santer told Corriere della Sera newspaper that budget plans unveiled last week removed many doubts.

"I have absolute faith that Germany, France and now even Italy, after the latest decisions of the Italian government in its economic programme, will successfully prepare themselves to respect the euro criteria," Santer was quoted as saying.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi announced last week that the government's 1998 budget would slice 25 trillion lire off the deficit through a mix of spending cuts and fresh revenue.
He said this would reduce next year's deficit to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) from the planned 3.0 percent this year and 6.7 percent in 1996.
"If the economic results meet political intentions, then there will be no reason for Italy not to qualify for entry into the euro from January 1, 1999," Santer said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
